title: Planetary Science and Scientific Information Systems
blurb: How observations of small bodies, moons, and planetary surfaces become durable, discoverable evidence.

person.name: Stephanie Jarmak
person.expertise: Planetary science, minor planets, comets, moons and satellites, granular mechanics, remote sensing, mission design, and scientific information systems

papers.title: Space missions on Solar System minor bodies

notes.takeaway: Mission encounters turn small bodies from points in a survey into measured worlds.
notes.why: It establishes the observational and engineering context for planetary small-body research.

papers.title: The geology and geophysics of Kuiper Belt object (486958) Arrokoth

notes.takeaway: Close imaging of Arrokoth preserves evidence about primitive bodies and early Solar System assembly.
notes.why: It shows how mission data revise population-level formation narratives.

papers.title: The OSIRIS-REx Spacecraft and the Touch-and-Go Sample Acquisition Mechanism (TAGSAM)

notes.takeaway: Sampling an asteroid requires spacecraft, surface, and granular-material knowledge to work together.
notes.why: It connects planetary science with the mechanics of interacting with regolith.

papers.title: ASIME 2018 White Paper: In-Space Utilisation of Asteroids

notes.takeaway: Asteroid composition links remote observations to questions about small-body evolution and in-space use.
notes.why: It provides a verified bridge from asteroid characterization to mission planning.

papers.title: Exocomets from a Solar System Perspective

notes.takeaway: Solar System comet observations give physical context for unresolved exocomet signatures.
notes.why: It shows how small-body science links local measurements to comparative planetary systems.

papers.title: Phobos photometic properties from Mars Express HRSC observations

notes.takeaway: Long-running spacecraft archives can reveal new surface information about a small satellite.
notes.why: It demonstrates the value of reusing mission data with improved questions.

papers.title: Ice-Ocean Exchange Processes in the Jovian and Saturnian Satellites

notes.takeaway: Ice-shell dynamics and ocean exchange connect surface observations to hidden interiors.
notes.why: It frames moons as evolving worlds rather than inert satellites.

papers.title: Ultraviolet-Based Science in the Solar System: Advances and Next Steps

notes.takeaway: Ultraviolet measurements reveal surface, atmospheric, and plasma processes that visible imaging misses.
notes.why: It broadens the remote-sensing toolkit used across planetary targets.

papers.title: Fundamental Characterisation of Planetary Surface Material in Microgravity Environments

notes.takeaway: Granular surface behavior must be characterized under the gravity and contact conditions of exploration.
notes.why: It connects granular mechanics to instruments and mission operations.

papers.title: An On-Orbit CubeSat Centrifuge for Asteroid Science and Exploration

notes.takeaway: Controlled gravity experiments can test how asteroid materials behave before committing to a large mission.
notes.why: It turns uncertain surface mechanics into an experimentally addressable question.

papers.title: Tudat: an open-source, high-fidelity orbit and parameter estimation software ─ Overview of planetary mission data analysis capabilities

notes.takeaway: Open computational tools make mission analysis and parameter estimation reproducible.
notes.why: Software provenance is part of the evidence chain in modern planetary science.

papers.title: OSIRIS-APEX: An OSIRIS-REx Extended Mission to Asteroid Apophis

notes.takeaway: An extended mission carries target identity, instruments, and data provenance from one asteroid encounter into the next.
notes.why: It is a concrete case for linking mission products and follow-up literature.

sections.label: From populations to visited worlds
sections.summary: Small-body science begins with populations and trajectories, then gains physical specificity when missions measure surfaces and sample regolith. Arrokoth and OSIRIS-REx show how formation questions become coupled to navigation, instruments, and contact mechanics.
questions: How should mission measurements update population-level formation models?

sections.label: Activity across taxonomies
sections.summary: Cometary dust and gas make taxonomy provisional: activity records changing volatiles, surfaces, and solar forcing. Comparative work uses Solar System comets as physical anchors for interpreting unresolved exocomets and active asteroids.
questions: Which observations distinguish volatile loss from impact or rotational activity?

sections.label: Satellites as evolving worlds
sections.summary: Phobos and the icy satellites show how long archives and interior models connect surface measurements to geological history. The central progression is from photometry and morphology toward coupled surface-interior processes.
questions: Which remote signatures most strongly constrain hidden interiors?

sections.label: Mechanics and multispectral evidence
sections.summary: UV observations add compositional and plasma information, while granular-mechanics experiments test how planetary materials behave under exploration conditions. Together they show that remote sensing and physical experiments must be interpreted as one evidence chain.
questions: How can laboratory mechanics be transferred to heterogeneous planetary surfaces?

sections.label: Frontier: mission design and reusable evidence
sections.summary: OSIRIS-APEX turns a close planetary encounter into a new experiment at Apophis, while open orbit-analysis tools support the interpretation of mission data. The frontier joins testable mission questions to reusable calculations and traceable data products.
questions: What provenance must travel with a planetary claim?
